turns.reply: Keep the fridge and freezer doors closed. With doors closed, food stays safe about 4 hours in the refrigerator, 48 hours in a full freezer, and 24 hours in a half-full freezer. turns.reply: Throw out perishable food (meat, fish, eggs, milk, leftovers, cut fruit and vegetables) that went more than 4 hours without power or a cold source, and anything with an unusual smell, color, or texture. Frozen food that still has ice crystals, or is at 40°F or below, can be refrozen or cooked. Never taste food to check it. When in doubt, throw it out.

turns.reply: Throw out perishable food (meat, fish, eggs, milk, leftovers, cut fruit and vegetables) that went more than 4 hours without power or a cold source, and anything with an unusual smell, color, or texture. Replace lost fluids now: water, plus electrolytes if you have them. Get medical help right away for confusion, fainting, no urine, a racing heartbeat, fast breathing, or shock. Other signs: strong thirst, dry mouth, dark urine, dizziness, tiredness. In babies and young children: crying without tears, no wet diaper for 3 hours or more, sunken eyes, unusual sleepiness. Oral rehydration solutions are made for children.
(Shown first in case someone needs help now.)

turns.reply: There is no fixed number. In heat or during hard work, an adult can sweat 1 to 1.5 liters an hour, and dehydration can turn dangerous within hours. Children are more at risk. A resting adult in comfortable surroundings may last a week or more with little or no water. Stay cool, rest, and avoid alcohol: it makes dehydration worse.
turns.say: How long can you live without drinking water?

turns.reply: Heat stroke is an emergency: 103°F or higher, hot red skin, confusion, or passing out. Call 911, move them somewhere cooler, cool them with cool cloths or a cool bath, and give nothing to drink. Heat exhaustion (heavy sweating, cold clammy skin, dizziness, nausea): move to a cool place, loosen clothes, use cool wet cloths, sip water. Get help if vomiting, worse, or over an hour.
turns.say: After working outside in the heat, my dad is confused and his skin is hot.

turns.reply: Hypothermia is a medical emergency. Signs: shivering, exhaustion, confusion, fumbling hands, slurred speech, drowsiness; in babies, bright red cold skin and very low energy. Below 95°F, get medical help now. Move them somewhere warm, remove wet clothes, and warm the chest, neck, head and groin first. Warm drinks help, but no alcohol, and nothing to drink if unconscious.
turns.say: She came in from the cold shivering and slurring her words.

turns.reply: Get medical care as soon as you can. Move them somewhere warm, remove wet clothes, and cover them with dry blankets. Rewarm the area in water that feels warm, not hot, to the touch. Don't rub it, don't walk on frostbitten feet unless you must, and don't warm it with a heating pad, electric blanket, fireplace, heat lamp, radiator, or stove. Signs: numbness, white or grayish-yellow skin, firm or waxy skin.
turns.say: My fingertips are white and numb after being out in the cold.

turns.reply: Hypothermia is a medical emergency. Signs: shivering, exhaustion, confusion, fumbling hands, slurred speech, drowsiness; in babies, bright red cold skin and very low energy. Below 95°F, get medical help now. Move them somewhere warm, remove wet clothes, and warm the chest, neck, head and groin first. Warm drinks help, but no alcohol, and nothing to drink if unconscious.
turns.say: my son is shivering and his speech is slurred

turns.reply: Insulin vials and cartridges can stay unrefrigerated between 59°F and 86°F for up to 28 days and still work. Keep it out of direct heat and sunlight. Don't use insulin that has frozen. In an emergency you may need to use insulin stored above 86°F; replace it with properly stored insulin as soon as you can. Throw away pump insulin exposed to over 98.6°F.

turns.reply: Keep the fridge and freezer doors closed. With doors closed, food stays safe about 4 hours in the refrigerator, 48 hours in a full freezer, and 24 hours in a half-full freezer. After 4 hours without power, move perishable food from the fridge into a cooler with ice. Never taste food to check it.

turns.reply: Get medical care as soon as you can. Move them somewhere warm, remove wet clothes, and cover them with dry blankets. Rewarm the area in water that feels warm, not hot, to the touch. Don't rub it, don't walk on frostbitten feet unless you must, and don't warm it with a heating pad, electric blanket, fireplace, heat lamp, radiator, or stove. Signs: numbness, white or grayish-yellow skin, firm or waxy skin.

turns.reply: Replace lost fluids now: water, plus electrolytes if you have them. Get medical help right away for confusion, fainting, no urine, a racing heartbeat, fast breathing, or shock. Other signs: strong thirst, dry mouth, dark urine, dizziness, tiredness. In babies and young children: crying without tears, no wet diaper for 3 hours or more, sunken eyes, unusual sleepiness. Oral rehydration solutions are made for children.
